subject: Discovery: AuroraPay pilot — benchmark plan, parity gating & next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Susan Li <susan.li@aurorapay.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@aurorapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + benchmark artifacts / next steps

Hi Susan / Raj — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope for the pilot: 

1) Goal: Validate parity of an open model constellation vs AuroraPay's in-house baseline on payment FAQ + transaction classification workflows (customer-facing support).

2) What we need from AuroraPay:
   - A de-identified eval slice (~1,000 examples) covering: multi-turn FAQ queries, ambiguous transaction descriptions, and edge-case refunds.
   - A short doc describing your baseline metrics (F1 for intent, exact-match for templated responses, and latest hallucination audit).

3) Redwood will provide:
   - Proposed benchmark plan and prompt sets (attached: aurorapay_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx, prompt-set-payment-faqs.jsonl).
   - Shortlist of open models to trial plus a test harness and evaluation script.

4) Acceptance / parity proposal (draft):
   - Primary quality gate: end-task F1 within 2 percentage points of your baseline, AND hallucination rate delta <= 1.5 percentage points.
   - Latency gate: p95 infer latency <= 350ms for the recommended config.
   - If quality delta is 0–2% but hallucination delta >1.5%, we run targeted prompt/regeneration trials before escalating.

Action items:
 - Susan: confirm you can upload a de-id eval set to the Drive link below by 2027-03-24.
 - Raj: share the baseline metric snapshot (or a short export) by EOD 2027-03-18.
 - Marissa / Dev / Karthik: we’ll prepare the harness + initial model runs once data arrives.

Attachments: aurorapay_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx (xlsx), prompt-set-payment-faqs.jsonl (jsonl)

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30m check-in for next Wed (suggested: 2027-03-24) to review the initial runs.

—
Jasmine Liu

jasmine.liu@redwood.com

Date: 2027-03-17T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + benchmark artifacts / next steps

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the tidy recap. Quick notes from our side: 

- We can get you a de-identified eval slice by 2027-03-24 (legal & privacy teams are reviewing but expect green).
- Baseline snapshot: our in-house model (PayNet-Prod v2) reports: intent F1 0.815, templated-response exact-match 0.62, hallucination audit 2.8% across the sampled set. I’ll try to export the exact artifacts; Raj will ping with a link.
- Concern: we are particularly sensitive to hallucinations on refund flows (regulatory/chargeback risk). If an open model shows lower latency but slightly higher hallucination, we may still prefer a conservative rollout.

We agree with the draft gates but can we add an explicit safety check: if hallucination rate >3.5% on any refund-specific slice, automatically fail parity? Otherwise good to proceed.

—
Susan Li
CTO, AuroraPay
susan.li@aurorapay.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + benchmark artifacts / next steps

Looping in our evaluation plan and a short model shortlist — keeping this practical so we can iterate quickly after you upload the eval set.

Shortlist (initial):
- LlamaX-13B-qlora (recommended config: 13B q4f16 - good for instruction-following, strong long-context answers)
- Redstone-7B-q4 (smaller, faster; good for low-cost A/B runs)
- Orca-Base-13B (for comparison; sometimes better on multi-turn coherence)

Why these: they balance token-efficiency and instruction-following for FAQ-style flows. We will run both direct prompting and a few constrained-generation templates that match PayNet-Prod’s response schema.

Proposed parity gating (concrete):
- Primary metric: Task F1 (intent+slot extraction aggregated) — pass if F1 >= (baseline F1 - 0.02).
- Hallucination: measured via labeled hallucination flags on the eval set — fail if overall hallucination rate > 3.5% OR refund-slice hallucination > 3.5%.
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms on Aurora’s target instance type; if p95 is between 350–450ms we can consider caching/prefix-KV strategies as mitigation but require a mitigation plan.
- Cost parity: optional — report tokens/second and estimated $/1M requests. Not a hard gate for pilot.

Benchmarks & assets we’ll run:
- QA harness (open-source runner) with at least 3 prompt templates (attached prompt-set-payment-faqs.jsonl).
- SARI / exact-match for templated responses; F1 for intent; hallucination audit sampling protocol (10% sample with manual verification).

If Aurora agrees to these gates, Dev and I will schedule the first run within 48h of data upload.

Related links: Test harness & runner: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuroraEvalUploads
—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

3) 2027-03-29: Internal QA sampling and hallucination audit complete.
4) 2027-03-30: 30m readout with Aurora — show parity metrics, highlight any refund-slice failures and mitigation proposals.
